subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 5: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
central_question: How can changes be classified by new-substance formation, reversibility, usefulness and natural processes, and what conditions are required for combustion?
in_scope_units: Activity 5.1 and everyday changes: observing changes in size, shape, state, smell and other properties.
5.1 A Substance May Change in Appearance but Remain the Same!: physical changes in paper, balloons, chalk and states of water.
5.2 A Substance May Change in Appearance and Not Remain the Same!: chemical changes, lime-water test and vinegar-baking soda reaction.
5.3 Some Other Processes Involving Chemical Changes: rusting and combustion.
Activities 5.5–5.6: oxygen requirement, ignition temperature and the fire triangle.
5.4 Can Physical and Chemical Changes Occur in the Same Process?: burning candle and Michael Faraday.
5.5 Are Changes Permanent?: reversible and irreversible changes.
5.6 Are All Changes Desirable?: desirable, undesirable and context-dependent changes and environmental effects.
5.7 Some Slow Natural Changes: weathering of rocks, soil formation, erosion, transport and deposition.
Let Us Enhance Our Learning: Questions 1–10 and exploratory projects.
banned_topics: Detailed atomic rearrangement and chemical bonding.

known_pitfalls.correction: Crushing chalk and chopping vegetables are physical changes that may not be practically reversible.

known_pitfalls.claim: Every colour change proves a chemical change.
known_pitfalls.correction: A chemical change is identified by formation of one or more new substances; colour change is evidence only when interpreted with the process.

known_pitfalls.claim: Air alone is enough for any combustible material to burn.
known_pitfalls.correction: Fuel, oxygen and heat sufficient to reach ignition temperature are all required.

known_pitfalls.claim: Only the wax melting occurs when a candle burns.
known_pitfalls.correction: Melting, flowing, solidification and evaporation are physical changes, while burning wax vapour is a chemical change.

known_pitfalls.claim: Weathering and erosion mean the same thing.
known_pitfalls.correction: Weathering breaks or chemically alters rocks, while erosion moves rock particles, soil and sediments.

recommended_example_progression: Use Activities 5.1–5.2 to introduce observations and physical changes.
Use Activities 5.3–5.4 to establish new-substance formation and the lime-water carbon-dioxide test.
Use Activities 5.5–5.6 to derive the requirements of combustion and ignition temperature.
Use Activity 5.7 to separate physical and chemical parts of candle burning.
Use Activity 5.8 to compare reversible and irreversible changes.
Use Let Us Enhance Our Learning Questions 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 10 for classification and evidence.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The section 'Let Us Enhance Our Learning' contains Questions 1–10, followed by several Exploratory Projects.
